metaDescription: Four Agri-Fab lawn sweepers compared: 44, 50 and 42 inch tow models plus a 30 inch push model, with hopper, brush and hitch advice for buyers.
expertTake: The 44 inch flow-through model is the top pick because its brush speed and bag design clear leaves fastest. The 42 inch model is the value pick for a smaller lawn and a smaller tractor. Skip the category if your trees drop wet, matted leaves, because no sweeper handles those well and a mulching mower or blower will serve you better.
introParagraphs: A lawn sweeper is a ground driven machine. A tractor or your own legs turn the wheels, a belt or chain spins the brushes, and the brushes flick debris into a bag. There is no engine to start and almost nothing to fail, which is why a good one lasts for decades.

Even so, buyers get tripped up by details the listing glosses over. Brush speed, bag shape, hopper size and working width all change how the machine behaves on a real yard. This guide explains those choices so the right size is obvious before you buy.

products.name: Agri-Fab 44 In Tow Sweeper, 28 Cu Ft Flow-Through
products.description:
This model leads the group because it pairs a large bag with a fast brush. Its 5.6 to 1 brush to wheel ratio means the brush turns more than five times for each wheel rotation, which flicks leaves, clippings and even pinecones into the hopper at ordinary tractor speed. The 28 cubic foot flow-through bag fills from back to front, so it uses its whole volume rather than packing the first few inches.

The tradeoff is size and tow demand. A full 28 cubic foot bag of damp leaves is heavy, and a small lawn tractor may struggle with it on a slope. Against the 42 inch model with a 12 cubic foot bag, you dump about half as often, but you need more storage room and a stronger tow vehicle.

Ownership is simple but not maintenance free. The bag fabric is the part that fades, tears and mildews first, so empty it and let it dry before storage.
products.bestFor: Tractor owners with a large leafy lawn who want fewer stops.

cons: A full bag is heavy for small tractors

products.name: Agri-Fab 50 In Heavy Duty Tow Sweeper, 26 Cu Ft
products.description:
The 50 inch model is the widest sweeper here, with a 50 inch working path inside a 58 inch overall frame. That width saves passes on open ground, and four 10 inch brushes with extra bristles keep more contact with the turf.

Width is also its main limit. At 58 inches overall it will not fit through many side gates, and tight orchard rows or flower beds make turning awkward. The 44 inch unit gives up 6 inches of working width but is easier to place, and it adds brush speed with its 5.6 to 1 ratio. If your yard is mostly open lawn, the wider path wins.

Expect the usual wear points. Bristles shorten with use, the hopper bag eventually tears, and the flat ground driven wheels can lose traction on wet turf.
products.bestFor: Acreage owners with open lawn and a tractor with real drawbar pull.
pros: 50 inch path saves passes on open ground
Four 10 in brushes keep strong turf contact
Heavy duty build suits larger jobs
cons: 58 inch overall width blocks many gates
Awkward in tight beds and corners
Needs a strong tractor with a full bag

products.name: Agri-Fab 42 In Tow Sweeper, 12 Cu Ft Hopper
products.description:
The 42 inch sweeper is the compact tow option, with a 42 inch sweeping width and a 12 cubic foot hopper bag. Its brush height adjustment lets the bristles reach as much as half an inch into the grass, which helps pick up clippings and small twigs. A rope dumps the bag, so you do not have to climb off the tractor for every load.

The main compromise is hopper size. At 12 cubic feet it holds less than half the volume of the 44 inch model, so a heavy leaf drop means frequent dumps. In return it is lighter to pull, which suits a small lawn tractor, and it is easier to store than the larger frames.

Owners should watch the rope and the bag. A thin rope can struggle with a wet packed load, and the bag fabric is the usual year-three failure. Dry the bag after emptying it and replace worn brushes before they stop picking up debris.
products.bestFor: Small to mid lawns with a lawn tractor and modest leaf volume.
pros: Lighter to tow behind a small tractor
Brush height reaches half an inch deep
Rope dump from the driver seat
Easier to store than larger frames
cons: 12 cu ft bag fills quickly in heavy fall
Rope can struggle with wet loads
Not a fit for acreage jobs

products.name: Agri-Fab 45-0570 30 In Push Behind Sweeper
products.description:
The 45-0570 is the only sweeper here that you push on foot. It has a 30 inch width, four brushes and a 12 cubic foot bag, which is as large as the 42 inch tow unit's. An adjustable brush height lets you set the bristles to the thickness of your turf.

Because you supply the power, it suits a small yard with no tractor. A 30 inch path covers about 70 percent of what the 42 inch tow model does per pass, and you walk every foot of it, so large lawns are unrealistic. Mowing first helps, since short grass releases clippings and leaves more cleanly.

Ownership is easy, with no engine and a compact storage footprint. Empty the bag, dry it, and check the brushes for wear each season.
products.bestFor: Small yards where no tractor is available to tow a sweeper.
pros: Works with no tractor or hitch
12 cu ft bag matches the 42 inch tow unit
cons: Bag fills fast in heavy leaf fall

buyingCriteria.explanation: The ratio sets how fast the brushes spin relative to wheel speed, and faster brushes fling debris into the bag more reliably. The 44 inch model cites 5.6 to 1, which is at the high end of the typical 5 to 1 range. A low ratio at walking speed leaves leaves behind. The common mistake is buying on width alone while ignoring how the brush is driven.

Hoppers run from 12 cubic feet on the 42 inch and 30 inch units to 26 and 28 cubic feet on the 50 and 44 inch models. Bigger bags mean fewer dumps but a heavier machine, especially with wet leaves. A flow-through bag, as on the 44 and 50 inch models, fills back to front and uses its volume. Match bag size to your tractor's pull, not just your yard.

The 50 inch unit has a 50 inch working path but a 58 inch overall frame, so gate clearance depends on the larger number. Measure your narrowest gate and your tractor wheelbase. A wide sweeper saves passes on open lawn but is a nuisance in beds and corners. For lots with fences, the 42 inch tow or 30 inch push model fits more easily.

Brushes should just touch the turf tips, with penetration of about half an inch cited for the 42 inch model. Set too low, they drag, wear and stall the drive. Set too high, they skip clippings. Good adjustment lets you change the setting as the grass grows or after a mow.

A rope or lever lets you empty the bag from the seat, which matters when you dump a dozen times in an afternoon. The 42 inch model uses a rope, and thin ropes struggle with wet packed loads. Check that the hitch fits your tractor, zero turn or ATV, and that the tow bar does not flex on tight turns.

buyingCriteria.criterion: What a sweeper actually picks up
buyingCriteria.explanation: Sweepers collect dry leaves, grass clippings, pine needles, small cones and light twigs. Wet matted leaves clump and clog the brushes on every model here. Mow or mulch first, and sweep on a dry, calm day. If your yard mostly drops wet leaves, a blower or mulching mower is the better tool.

specDecoder.meaning: More and larger brushes mean more bristle contact with the turf. Contact is what lifts debris out of the grass.

howWeEvaluated.title: Pickup mechanism
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated how each sweeper turns wheel motion into brush speed, based on the spec sheet. The 44 inch model's 5.6 to 1 ratio set the benchmark. Models without a cited ratio were judged on brush count and contact.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and bag design
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared hopper volume and whether the bag fills efficiently. The 28 and 26 cubic foot flow-through bags ranked above the 12 cubic foot units for large jobs. Dump frequency was a scoring factor.

howWeEvaluated.title: Width and maneuvering
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed working width against overall width and gate clearance. The 50 inch unit scored high on coverage but lower on fit, since it measures 58 inches overall. Narrower models gained points for flexibility.

howWeEvaluated.title: Tow demand and ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered the tow vehicle needed and the upkeep burden. Bag fabric, brush wear and drive tension are the common year-three issues based on owner feedback patterns. Lighter machines suit smaller tractors.

howWeEvaluated.title: Honest fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched each machine to a realistic lawn size and leaf load. The 30 inch push unit fits only small yards, while the 44 inch fits large leafy ones. Fit outweighed raw specs.

cards.label: Tow behind
cards.text: Tow models hitch to a tractor, zero turn or ATV, so the vehicle does the work and you cover ground quickly. They carry bigger bags of 12 to 28 cubic feet and dump from the seat. The 44, 50 and 42 inch units fall here.

cards.label: Push behind
cards.text: A push sweeper needs no tow vehicle and stores easily, but you walk every pass. It suits small yards and spot work. The 30 inch 45-0570 is the only push model in this group.

howToChoose.note: Pick a tow model if you own a tractor and have more than a quarter acre. Choose the 30 inch push model only for a small yard.

howToChoose.subheading: For Heavy Fall Leaf Cleanup Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a large flow-through bag and a high brush to wheel ratio, since a tree-heavy yard fills small bags in minutes. A strong tow vehicle matters because a full bag of leaves is heavy. Mow first so leaves are shredded and pack more densely.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Agri-Fab 44 In Tow Sweeper with a 28 cu ft flow-through bag and a 5.6 to 1 ratio is the best fit. The 50 inch unit is the choice if the lawn is wide and open.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more on the 44 inch or 50 inch tow model if you have a big yard, a capable tractor and many trees. The larger bags and faster brush speed cut hours from the job. The extra frame also tends to hold up better under heavy loads.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save with the 42 inch tow or 30 inch push model if your yard is small or your leaf load is light. A smaller machine is easier to store and tow. A blower may beat all of them if your leaves are wet.

maintenance.why: Damp debris breeds mildew and rots the fabric. A dry bag lasts noticeably longer.
Worn bristles lose contact with the turf and stop picking up debris. Replace brushes before pickup falls off.
A loose belt or chain slips and slows the brush. Lubricate where the design allows.
Vibration loosens bolts on a ground driven frame. A loose pin can drop the sweeper behind your tractor.
Low tires change brush height and traction. Look for cracks or bent tubing on the hopper frame.

faq.q: Should I buy a tow behind or a push sweeper?
faq.a: Buy a tow model if you own a tractor and have more than a quarter acre. Push sweepers suit small yards with no tow vehicle. A 30 inch push path means many more passes.

faq.q: How much should I budget for an Agri-Fab sweeper?
faq.a: The push unit is at the low end and the large flow-through models cost the most. Spend more only if your yard is large and leafy, since a small lawn gains little from a bigger bag.

faq.q: How long does a lawn sweeper last?
faq.a: The frame often outlasts the fabric. Bags tear and fade first, and brushes wear with use. With dry storage and replacement parts, a sweeper can work for many years.

faq.q: Does a higher brush to wheel ratio really matter?
faq.a: Yes, because faster brush tips move more debris at the same tow speed. The 44 inch model cites 5.6 to 1. Walking speed is the limit for push units.

faq.q: Can a sweeper pick up wet leaves?
faq.a: Not well. Wet matted leaves clump, clog the brushes and overload the bag. Wait for a dry day or use a blower.

faq.q: Will a sweeper fit through my gate?
faq.a: Check the overall width, not the working width. The 50 inch unit is 58 inches overall. Measure the narrowest gate before ordering.
